concerns.text: T018a (Derive Group) and T018f (Clean) are marked [X] (complete) but explicitly list dependencies on T018c/d/e/g (Fetch) which are marked [ ] (incomplete/failed). This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' rule: downstream tasks cannot be complete if their upstream data producers are missing.

T017 (Validate Data Gap) is marked [ ] (incomplete) but depends on T018c/d/e/g (Fetch). The logical flow requires Fetch -> Gap Check -> Clean. Currently, the Gap Check is blocked by missing fetch tasks, yet the Clean task (T018f) is marked complete, creating a circular/invalid dependency chain where cleaning happens before gap validation.

T018b (Compute Range Uncertainty) is marked [X] (complete) but depends on T018f (Clean) which processes `range_original`. While T018f is marked complete, the upstream fetch tasks (T018c/d/e/g) required to populate `range_original` are missing. The artifact flow is broken: no raw data -> no range_original -> no uncertainty calculation.

T020 (Validate No Missing Primary Predictors) is marked [ ] (incomplete) and depends on T019a/b/c (Descriptors). T019 depends on T018f (Clean). Since T018f depends on missing Fetch tasks, the entire US1 implementation chain is logically broken. The task list claims partial completion of a pipeline that cannot execute.

T018d and T018e descriptions contain 'FAILED: unspecified' comments and empty URL placeholders. While this is a content issue, it directly impacts the 'Producer' status of these tasks. They cannot be considered 'ready' producers until the source URLs are defined, breaking the dependency chain for T017/T018a/T018f.
